semesters.title: Mathematical foundations
semesters.subtitle: Probability, statistics and optimization, plus deep-learning basics built from scratch, before the LLM semesters

semesters.title: Language models from first principles
semesters.subtitle: CS336, Raschka's LLM book, scaling, plus the ML and maths foundations

semesters.title: Reinforcement learning, post-training and reasoning
semesters.subtitle: CS285 and CS224R, the RLHF book, Raschka's reasoning book, concentration inequalities

semesters.title: Generative models and 3D vision
semesters.subtitle: Flow matching, diffusion and Stable Diffusion from scratch; NeRF and Gaussian splatting

semesters.title: Agents, RAG, physical AI and online learning
semesters.subtitle: CMU 11-768 as the spine, Berkeley's MOOCs, RAG, robot learning, bandits and online learning

semesters.title: Mathematics for research: proofs, matrix analysis and online learning
semesters.subtitle: Proof writing, advanced linear algebra and matrix calculus, matrix perturbation and concentration, deep learning theory, information theory, SDEs, optimal transport, and a deep online-learning track

semesters.title: Learning theory, probabilistic and unsupervised learning, game theory
semesters.subtitle: MIT 9.520, Hennig's probabilistic ML, Berkeley's Deep Unsupervised Learning, Ghodsi's unsupervised course, Polak and Roughgarden on games

semesters.title: Decision-making and language
semesters.subtitle: CS234, CS885, Bertsekas's approximate DP and RL courses, Sutton & Barto exercises, Jurafsky & Manning, CMU Advanced NLP 2024, CS25, bio-inspired AI

semesters.title: Vision, graphs, meta- and continual learning
semesters.subtitle: Geiger's Computer Vision, Cremers's variational methods, NUS 3D vision, TUM CV3DST, CS224W, CS330, ContinualAI; ends with the program finals

semesters.title: Learning paradigms and perception
semesters.subtitle: Self- and semi-supervised learning, zero-/few-shot and multi-task learning, domain generalization, uncertainty, detection/segmentation/tracking from classic to modern, and text-to-3D

semesters.title: Bayesian, geometric and generative frontiers
semesters.subtitle: Bayesian ML following Punit Rathore's IISc syllabus, Bayesian optimization, geometric deep learning, advanced flow matching, diffusion language models and Gaussian splatting

semesters.title: Efficient ML and ML systems
semesters.subtitle: Pruning, quantization and distillation in depth (CNNs, ViTs, LLMs, VLMs), autodiff frameworks, GPU kernels, LLM serving and MLOps

semesters.title: Architectures, multimodality, interpretability, safety and evaluation
semesters.subtitle: State-space models and long context, vision-language models, mechanistic interpretability, safety and red-teaming, and rigorous LLM evaluation

semesters.title: Causality, science, speech and time series
semesters.subtitle: Causal inference and causal representation learning, AI for science (molecules, neural operators, weather), speech and audio, and time-series foundation models

semesters.title: Applied AI engineering
semesters.subtitle: The Udemy tracks and audited Coursera courses, then MLOps, LLM and agent apps, Google's agent intensive, loop engineering and a phone app; ends with the whole-program finals
